Proven product leader to advance Forma industry cloud and AI strategy and drive the next phase of AEC growth
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADSK) today announced that Diana Colella has been named executive vice president of its architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) business. Colella succeeds Amy Bunszel, who previously announced her retirement and will remain with Autodesk through November 2, 2026, to support the transition.
Colella will lead Autodesk's largest industry business as the company enters its next phase of growth in AEC, driven by Autodesk Forma, the company's industry cloud for AEC that connects data, context and workflows to deliver AI and project intelligence across the AEC lifecycle.
"The AEC industry is entering a new era, as AI creates new possibilities for how buildings and infrastructure are designed, built and operated," said Andrew Anagnost, president and CEO of Autodesk. "Amy and the AEC team have built a strong business and laid the foundation for the next phase of growth, with Forma becoming the industry cloud for AEC and AI helping customers navigate increasing complexity across the project lifecycle. Diana is the right leader for this moment. She brings a proven track record of leading through major technology shifts, aligning products, data and teams behind a clear vision, and turning innovation into tangible customer outcomes. Combined with her deep understanding of Autodesk and the industries we serve, Diana is uniquely positioned to build on this momentum and help shape the future of AEC."
p>In her new role, Colella will advance the Forma strategy while continuing to evolve our desktop products such as Revit and Civil 3D while connecting them more closely to Forma workflows. By bringing together the data and context created across the project lifecycle, Autodesk aims to make AI more useful in the work customers do every day, helping teams reduce friction, make better-informed decisions and increase their capacity to design and build.
Colella brings nearly three decades of Autodesk leadership experience spanning finance, strategy, sales, operations, product management and industry leadership. She joined Autodesk through the acquisition of Discreet Logic and has since held leadership roles across the company, including leading Autodesk's AutoCAD business and helping launch One AutoCAD. Her broad experience has given her deep insight into how Autodesk's products, operations and go-to-market teams work together to create customer success.
Most recently, Colella led the AI transformation of Autodesk's Media & Entertainment (M&E) business, where she advanced the Flow platform strategy and expanded Autodesk's role across the production lifecycle. Through acquisitions including Moxion, PIX and Wonder Dynamics, and the continued development of Autodesk Flow Studio, she helped broaden the value Autodesk delivers to creators and studios. Colella will continue to oversee the M&E business and will open a search for a new leader, reporting directly to her.
"Our customers are being asked to deliver more while navigating greater complexity, persistent resource constraints and rapid technological change," said Colella. "My priority is to listen to them, build on the strong foundation Amy and the team have created, and make sure the work we're doing across Forma and AI translates into meaningful improvements in how projects are designed, built and operated. I'm honored to lead Autodesk's AEC business at such an important moment for our customers and the industry."
The world's designers, engineers, builders, and creators trust Autodesk to help them design and make anything. From the buildings we live and work in, to the cars we drive and the bridges we drive over. From the products we use and rely on, to the movies and games that inspire us. Autodesk's Design and Make Platform unlocks the power of data to accelerate insights and automate processes, empowering customers with the technology to create the world around us and deliver better outcomes for their businesses and the planet. Autodesk (ADSK) vs. PTC and TRMB: Can Cloud and AI Investments Drive Faster Earnings Growth?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 11:43 AM CDT 7 min read
Is ADSK a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Autodesk, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. The thesis was published on September 11th, when the stock was trading at $212.40, and ADSK gained 9.95% since then. The gain appears to reflect optimism around Autodesk's new AI capabilities and renewed takeover interest in design software following Schneider Electric's announced acquisition of PTC. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ADSK. Autodesk, Inc.'s share was trading at $233.54 as of October 12th 2026. ADSK's trailing and forward P/E were 28.45 and 17.61 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.
This isn't the first time we see a software company pitched as a great investment. Software stocks have suffered steep declines over the past year, but does ADSK's recent recovery make this a good time to buy?

In June, we published an article about the 10 Oversold Stocks Offering High Upside and ADSK ranked #7 in that article. Btw, the #1 stock in that list returned 29.89% since then. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick and ADSK rewarded their bullish stance with a 25.21% gain over the same period. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ADSK. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADSK) provides 3D design, engineering, construction, manufacturing, and entertainment software through products such as AutoCAD, Revit, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Fusion, and Maya. Its shift toward cloud-based tools and artificial intelligence matters because these products are becoming more deeply built into how architects, engineers, manufacturers, and construction firms work.

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential
Revenue climbed 17.9% year over year to $7.8 billion, and Autodesk runs a highly profitable business, with a 92.5% gross margin, a 21.1% net margin, and a strong 36.9% return on equity. Even so, the stock trades at about 25 times forward earnings, a valuation that assumes steady subscription growth continues, leaving little room for setbacks like weaker construction spending, slower manufacturing activity, or fewer new customer sign-ups.
The bullish case is that Autodesk is becoming harder for customers to leave, as Revit, Fusion, and Autodesk Construction Cloud shift toward shared, cloud-based platforms. Instead of using separate desktop software, customers can now collaborate around one central project, which raises switching costs and gives Autodesk more room to sell additional products into its existing customer base. At the same time, AI-driven design tools could make customers more productive and support further growth within larger accounts. Autodesk's already-high margins and strong returns suggest real operating leverage — meaning profits could grow faster than revenue — as long as subscriptions, renewals, and enterprise expansion keep holding up.
Management is backing this strategy with a 7% workforce reduction, cutting about 1,000 jobs, and redirecting that spending toward cloud infrastructure and AI. Autodesk is also changing how it sells software: rather than resellers handling the full transaction, deals will now settle directly between Autodesk and the customer, giving the company more control over renewals and pricing. Financially, Autodesk generated about $2.4 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year and holds roughly $677 million more cash than debt, giving it flexibility to keep investing. For next fiscal year, management expects earnings per share between $7.89 and $8.72, and the company has beaten Wall Street's profit estimates in each of its last four quarters.
Wall Street's average price target of $315.37, based on 34 analysts, implies the stock could rise about 53% from its current price of $206.62. But reaching that target would mean Autodesk trading at nearly 38 times earnings, well above its current 25 times multiple. For the stock to hit $315.37 while keeping today's valuation steady, earnings per share would need to jump to around $12.67 — about 64% higher than current levels. Since profits aren't yet close to that mark, investors should watch whether earnings growth accelerates enough to justify that kind of price target. You can check out why Berenberg sees more upside in Autodesk despite key AI headwinds here.
The biggest risk is a slowdown in commercial real estate, construction, or manufacturing. Higher borrowing costs can delay building projects and reduce new construction starts, which would slow demand for Autodesk's design software, while weaker industrial activity could cause manufacturers to pull back spending too. The company also carries more debt than equity, and its current ratio of 0.85 means it has fewer short-term assets than short-term liabilities, leaving a thinner cushion despite its net cash position. Deeper cloud adoption also raises cybersecurity risk, since Autodesk's software often stores sensitive architectural and infrastructure designs. On top of that, cheaper CAD software in China and competitors like Bentley Systems Incorporated (NASDAQ:BSY) add pricing pressure in some markets. Together, these risks leave little room for error if growth slows.
Another risk for the stock is that its new sales model could make revenue growth look stronger than the underlying business. Autodesk now records partner incentives as operating costs rather than deductions from revenue. This raises reported revenue without necessarily bringing in more customer spending. Autodesk says the change boosts calculated revenue growth while being broadly neutral to operating profit and free cash flow. Its valuation depends on genuine subscription growth and stronger earnings. Investors could overestimate that growth if they mistake accounting changes for increased demand. In our opinion, this could pressure Autodesk's price multiples if profit growth fails to match the headline revenue gains.
Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 51 hedge funds held Autodesk at the end of the second quarter, down from 67 in the previous quarter. That pullback suggests institutional investors turned more cautious on Autodesk despite its strong profitability and long-term growth potential. By comparison, PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC) was held by 45 hedge funds, up from 42, Bentley Systems Incorporated was held by 31 hedge funds, down from 38, and Trimble Inc. (NASDAQ:TRMB) was held by 46 hedge funds, up from 43. Institutional sentiment cooled more sharply toward Autodesk than toward its peers this quarter, even though Autodesk still held the highest total hedge fund ownership among the four companies.
Short interest data paints a relatively calm picture. Only 5.01% of Autodesk's float is sold short, well below PTC Inc. at 8.49% and Bentley Systems Incorporated at 7.95%, though slightly above Trimble Inc. at 4.89%. So even though hedge fund ownership fell, bearish bets against Autodesk remain lower than those against PTC and Bentley Systems — suggesting the debate around the stock centers less on the business deteriorating and more on whether its growth and margins can support its valuation.
ADSK's forward P/E is 17.61x. PTC Inc., Bentley Systems Incorporated, and Trimble Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 16.26x, 19.96x, and 13.97x, respectively. ADSK's own forward P/E was 22.17x on January 31, 2026, putting its current valuation approximately 21% below that level. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about weaker construction and manufacturing demand, competition, and whether cloud and AI investments will deliver stronger profits. However, the lower multiple makes Autodesk more attractive against its own history, while its premium to PTC and Trimble still requires dependable earnings growth. Autodesk, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share increased from $6.63 in fiscal 2023 to $10.43 in fiscal 2026, representing approximately 16% annual growth. We believe 17.61 times expected earnings is a reasonable valuation if growth continues near that pace, because rising profits could support share-price gains without investors needing to pay a higher multiple. If Autodesk can maintain subscription growth and turn cost savings into lasting profits, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite the risks from weaker customer spending and competition.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Autodesk, Inc. (ADSK) by Francesco Ferrari in March 2025, which highlighted the company's 93% recurring revenue, 92% gross margin, and strong free cash flow generation. ADSK's stock price has depreciated by approximately 5.98% since our coverage. We believe ADSK could be a good long-term investment, provided continued subscription growth and improving profitability justify its current valuation.
Autodesk, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. One Margin at PTC Does Not Come From Software:
Net margin at PTC is 41.43% and operating margin is 28.23%. Net margin above operating margin means profit arrived from below the operating line rather than from selling licences. The multiples carry the distortion. PTC trades at 18.72 times trailing earnings and 21.71 times forward.
A forward figure above the trailing one says this year's profit is not expected to repeat, which is the same fact stated as a forecast. Autodesk moves the other way, from 29.98 times trailing to 16.55 times forward. Return on assets is 11.54% at PTC against 11.47% at Autodesk, so the two use their asset bases almost identically.

Sustainability for PTC is now a question for its acquirer rather than for the market, since the price is agreed. On price, Autodesk is the cheaper stock on forward estimates at 16.55 times against 21.71, with a PEG ratio of 0.78 against 1.81.
Enterprise value to EBITDA is closer at 17.45 for PTC against 21.29, because that measure counts the $1.61 billion of debt. Short interest of 9.21% at PTC against 4.45% is unusual for a company with an agreed cash offer on the table.

Autodesk is the better business by every operating measure that matters. Revenue grew 16.10% against a 6.80% decline, earnings rose 57.20% against a 16.00% fall, and free cash flow of $2.80 billion is three times PTC's. However, PTC has an agreed $22.6 billion cash offer and Autodesk has nothing of the kind, which is why one fell 4.32% over twelve months and the other 25.73%. PTC's 41.43% net margin above a 28.23% operating margin is not repeatable. The number to watch is Autodesk's forward multiple, because 16.55 times is what the market pays for the grower nobody bid for.

Autodesk names Diana Colella to lead architecture, engineering and construction business
Proven product leader to advance Forma industry cloud and AI strategy and drive the next phase of AEC growth
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADSK) today announced that Diana Colella has been named executive vice president of its architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) business. Colella succeeds Amy Bunszel, who previously announced her retirement and will remain with Autodesk through November 2, 2026, to support the transition.
Colella will lead Autodesk's largest industry business as the company enters its next phase of growth in AEC, driven by Autodesk Forma, the company's industry cloud for AEC that connects data, context and workflows to deliver AI and project intelligence across the AEC lifecycle.
"The AEC industry is entering a new era, as AI creates new possibilities for how buildings and infrastructure are designed, built and operated," said Andrew Anagnost, president and CEO of Autodesk. "Amy and the AEC team have built a strong business and laid the foundation for the next phase of growth, with Forma becoming the industry cloud for AEC and AI helping customers navigate increasing complexity across the project lifecycle. Diana is the right leader for this moment. She brings a proven track record of leading through major technology shifts, aligning products, data and teams behind a clear vision, and turning innovation into tangible customer outcomes. Combined with her deep understanding of Autodesk and the industries we serve, Diana is uniquely positioned to build on this momentum and help shape the future of AEC."
In her new role, Colella will advance the Forma strategy while continuing to evolve our desktop products such as Revit and Civil 3D while connecting them more closely to Forma workflows. By bringing together the data and context created across the project lifecycle, Autodesk aims to make AI more useful in the work customers do every day, helping teams reduce friction, make better-informed decisions and increase their capacity to design and build.
Colella brings nearly three decades of Autodesk leadership experience spanning finance, strategy, sales, operations, product management and industry leadership. She joined Autodesk through the acquisition of Discreet Logic and has since held leadership roles across the company, including leading Autodesk's AutoCAD business and helping launch One AutoCAD. Her broad experience has given her deep insight into how Autodesk's products, operations and go-to-market teams work together to create customer success.
Most recently, Colella led the AI transformation of Autodesk's Media & Entertainment (M&E) business, where she advanced the Flow platform strategy and expanded Autodesk's role across the production lifecycle. Through acquisitions including Moxion, PIX and Wonder Dynamics, and the continued development of Autodesk Flow Studio, she helped broaden the value Autodesk delivers to creators and studios. Colella will continue to oversee the M&E business and will open a search for a new leader, reporting directly to her.
"Our customers are being asked to deliver more while navigating greater complexity, persistent resource constraints and rapid technological change," said Colella. "My priority is to listen to them, build on the strong foundation Amy and the team have created, and make sure the work we're doing across Forma and AI translates into meaningful improvements in how projects are designed, built and operated. I'm honored to lead Autodesk's AEC business at such an important moment for our customers and the industry."
The world's designers, engineers, builders, and creators trust Autodesk to help them design and make anything. From the buildings we live and work in, to the cars we drive and the bridges we drive over. From the products we use and rely on, to the movies and games that inspire us. Autodesk's Design and Make Platform unlocks the power of data to accelerate insights and automate processes, empowering customers with the technology to create the world around us and deliver better outcomes for their businesses and the planet. Is Autodesk Still The Best Way To Own Faster Software Growth?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:52 PM CDT 4 min read
Autodesk (ADSK) stock lost 24.9% over the past year, while shares of Fair Isaac (FICO) fell 56.4%. Underneath those market declines, however, business at both software companies is accelerating. Each firm has posted faster sales growth in each of the past two years, and buyers of either stock are likely betting on that continued momentum. The similarities end there. The two companies operate with completely different financial structures. Fair Isaac retains far more of its sales as profit, yet Autodesk carries substantially less debt. So which of the two does the evidence favor?
In August, Autodesk Gave A Mixed Outlook
On August 27, Autodesk adjusted its expectations for the fiscal year ending in January 2027. The company raised its revenue forecast to a midpoint of $8.32 billion, up from $8.19 billion, and also increased its billings forecast. At the same time, it lowered its reported operating margin forecast down to 26.0% at the midpoint, from 27.0%.
Fair Isaac delivered a uniformly positive update on July 29, 2026. The company raised every forecast it gave for revenue, net income and earnings per share. For the fiscal year that ended in September 2026, management guided for $2.53 billion in revenue. Final results for that period are still to come.
Those optimistic projections arrived two months before a major industry announcement.
On September 28, the Federal Housing Finance Agency said the mortgage pricing grid is being simplified and that VantageScore is being incorporated. Fair Isaac stock fell after that statement the next day.
Autodesk Keeps Less Of Each Dollar, Holds More Cash
Looking at profitability, the two businesses operate in different tiers. Autodesk turned 27.9% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to July 2026. By contrast, Fair Isaac converted 52.1% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to June 2026.
When evaluating the balance sheet, Autodesk holds a commanding advantage. As of July 31, 2026, the company held $4.16 billion in cash and short-term investments, which easily exceeded its $3.71 billion of debt. Fair Isaac sits in a much tighter position. At June 30, 2026, the company owed $5.6 billion in debt against just $248 million of cash and short-term investments.
Fair Isaac trades at a notable discount relative to its bottom line. The stock trades at 20.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months. Investors are paying a higher premium for Autodesk, which trades at 29.6 times trailing earnings.
The top line also favors Fair Isaac. The company expanded sales by 24.1% over the twelve months to June 2026, easily outpacing the 17.9% growth Autodesk recorded over the twelve months to July 2026. Expanding the timeline reveals a similar pattern. Over its last three twelve-month periods, Fair Isaac averaged 17.7% growth, compared to 14.4% for Autodesk.
Autodesk reclaims the advantage regarding debt. The company carries debt equal to 7.6% of its market value. That sits well below the 34.4% ratio for Fair Isaac.
Based on its earnings multiple, growth, margin and forecasts, Fair Isaac comes out ahead, while Autodesk owes far less. The key variable remains timing. Fair Isaac issued its results and forecasts entirely before the agency's September move. The company expects to release its first report since that development on or around November 11, 2026. You should watch what Fair Isaac says about revenue in that report.

Is ADSK a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Autodesk, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. The thesis was published on September 11th, when the stock was trading at $212.40, and ADSK gained 9.95% since then. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADSK) provides 3D design, engineering, construction, manufacturing, and entertainment software through products such as AutoCAD, Revit, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Fusion, and Maya. Its shift toward cloud-based tools and artificial intelligence matters because these products are becoming more deeply built into how architects, engineers, manufacturers, and construction firms work.

Revenue climbed 17.9% year over year to $7.8 billion, and Autodesk runs a highly profitable business, with a 92.5% gross margin, a 21.1% net margin, and a strong 36.9% return on equity. Even so, the stock trades at about 25 times forward earnings, a valuation that assumes steady subscription growth continues, leaving little room for setbacks like weaker construction spending, slower manufacturing activity, or fewer new customer sign-ups.
The bullish case is that Autodesk is becoming harder for customers to leave, as Revit, Fusion, and Autodesk Construction Cloud shift toward shared, cloud-based platforms. Instead of using separate desktop software, customers can now collaborate around one central project, which raises switching costs and gives Autodesk more room to sell additional products into its existing customer base. At the same time, AI-driven design tools could make customers more productive and support further growth within larger accounts. Autodesk's already-high margins and strong returns suggest real operating leverage — meaning profits could grow faster than revenue — as long as subscriptions, renewals, and enterprise expansion keep holding up.
Management is backing this strategy with a 7% workforce reduction, cutting about 1,000 jobs, and redirecting that spending toward cloud infrastructure and AI. Autodesk is also changing how it sells software: rather than resellers handling the full transaction, deals will now settle directly between Autodesk and the customer, giving the company more control over renewals and pricing. Financially, Autodesk generated about $2.4 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year and holds roughly $677 million more cash than debt, giving it flexibility to keep investing. For next fiscal year, management expects earnings per share between $7.89 and $8.72, and the company has beaten Wall Street's profit estimates in each of its last four quarters.
Wall Street's average price target of $315.37, based on 34 analysts, implies the stock could rise about 53% from its current price of $206.62. But reaching that target would mean Autodesk trading at nearly 38 times earnings, well above its current 25 times multiple. For the stock to hit $315.37 while keeping today's valuation steady, earnings per share would need to jump to around $12.67 — about 64% higher than current levels. Since profits aren't yet close to that mark, investors should watch whether earnings growth accelerates enough to justify that kind of price target. The biggest risk is a slowdown in commercial real estate, construction, or manufacturing. Higher borrowing costs can delay building projects and reduce new construction starts, which would slow demand for Autodesk's design software, while weaker industrial activity could cause manufacturers to pull back spending too. The company also carries more debt than equity, and its current ratio of 0.85 means it has fewer short-term assets than short-term liabilities, leaving a thinner cushion despite its net cash position. Deeper cloud adoption also raises cybersecurity risk, since Autodesk's software often stores sensitive architectural and infrastructure designs. On top of that, cheaper CAD software in China and competitors like Bentley Systems Incorporated (NASDAQ:BSY) add pricing pressure in some markets. Together, these risks leave little room for error if growth slows.
Another risk for the stock is that its new sales model could make revenue growth look stronger than the underlying business. Autodesk now records partner incentives as operating costs rather than deductions from revenue. This raises reported revenue without necessarily bringing in more customer spending. Autodesk says the change boosts calculated revenue growth while being broadly neutral to operating profit and free cash flow. Its valuation depends on genuine subscription growth and stronger earnings. Investors could overestimate that growth if they mistake accounting changes for increased demand. In our opinion, this could pressure Autodesk's price multiples if profit growth fails to match the headline revenue gains.
Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 51 hedge funds held Autodesk at the end of the second quarter, down from 67 in the previous quarter. That pullback suggests institutional investors turned more cautious on Autodesk despite its strong profitability and long-term growth potential. By comparison, PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC) was held by 45 hedge funds, up from 42, Bentley Systems Incorporated was held by 31 hedge funds, down from 38, and Trimble Inc. (NASDAQ:TRMB) was held by 46 hedge funds, up from 43. Institutional sentiment cooled more sharply toward Autodesk than toward its peers this quarter, even though Autodesk still held the highest total hedge fund ownership among the four companies.
Short interest data paints a relatively calm picture. Only 5.01% of Autodesk's float is sold short, well below PTC Inc. at 8.49% and Bentley Systems Incorporated at 7.95%, though slightly above Trimble Inc. at 4.89%. So even though hedge fund ownership fell, bearish bets against Autodesk remain lower than those against PTC and Bentley Systems — suggesting the debate around the stock centers less on the business deteriorating and more on whether its growth and margins can support its valuation.
ADSK's forward P/E is 17.61x. PTC Inc., Bentley Systems Incorporated, and Trimble Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 16.26x, 19.96x, and 13.97x, respectively. ADSK's own forward P/E was 22.17x on January 31, 2026, putting its current valuation approximately 21% below that level. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about weaker construction and manufacturing demand, competition, and whether cloud and AI investments will deliver stronger profits. However, the lower multiple makes Autodesk more attractive against its own history, while its premium to PTC and Trimble still requires dependable earnings growth. Autodesk, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share increased from $6.63 in fiscal 2023 to $10.43 in fiscal 2026, representing approximately 16% annual growth. We believe 17.61 times expected earnings is a reasonable valuation if growth continues near that pace, because rising profits could support share-price gains without investors needing to pay a higher multiple. If Autodesk can maintain subscription growth and turn cost savings into lasting profits, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite the risks from weaker customer spending and competition.

Proven product leader to advance Forma industry cloud and AI strategy and drive the next phase of AEC growth
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADSK) today announced that Diana Colella has been named executive vice president of its architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) business. Colella succeeds Amy Bunszel, who previously announced her retirement and will remain with Autodesk through November 2, 2026, to support the transition.
Colella will lead Autodesk's largest industry business as the company enters its next phase of growth in AEC, driven by Autodesk Forma, the company's industry cloud for AEC that connects data, context and workflows to deliver AI and project intelligence across the AEC lifecycle.
"The AEC industry is entering a new era, as AI creates new possibilities for how buildings and infrastructure are designed, built and operated," said Andrew Anagnost, president and CEO of Autodesk. "Amy and the AEC team have built a strong business and laid the foundation for the next phase of growth, with Forma becoming the industry cloud for AEC and AI helping customers navigate increasing complexity across the project lifecycle. Diana is the right leader for this moment. She brings a proven track record of leading through major technology shifts, aligning products, data and teams behind a clear vision, and turning innovation into tangible customer outcomes. Combined with her deep understanding of Autodesk and the industries we serve, Diana is uniquely positioned to build on this momentum and help shape the future of AEC."
In her new role, Colella will advance the Forma strategy while continuing to evolve our desktop products such as Revit and Civil 3D while connecting them more closely to Forma workflows. By bringing together the data and context created across the project lifecycle, Autodesk aims to make AI more useful in the work customers do every day, helping teams reduce friction, make better-informed decisions and increase their capacity to design and build.
Colella brings nearly three decades of Autodesk leadership experience spanning finance, strategy, sales, operations, product management and industry leadership. She joined Autodesk through the acquisition of Discreet Logic and has since held leadership roles across the company, including leading Autodesk's AutoCAD business and helping launch One AutoCAD. Her broad experience has given her deep insight into how Autodesk's products, operations and go-to-market teams work together to create customer success.
Most recently, Colella led the AI transformation of Autodesk's Media & Entertainment (M&E) business, where she advanced the Flow platform strategy and expanded Autodesk's role across the production lifecycle. Through acquisitions including Moxion, PIX and Wonder Dynamics, and the continued development of Autodesk Flow Studio, she helped broaden the value Autodesk delivers to creators and studios. Colella will continue to oversee the M&E business and will open a search for a new leader, reporting directly to her.
"Our customers are being asked to deliver more while navigating greater complexity, persistent resource constraints and rapid technological change," said Colella. "My priority is to listen to them, build on the strong foundation Amy and the team have created, and make sure the work we're doing across Forma and AI translates into meaningful improvements in how projects are designed, built and operated. I'm honored to lead Autodesk's AEC business at such an important moment for our customers and the industry."
The world's designers, engineers, builders, and creators trust Autodesk to help them design and make anything. From the buildings we live and work in, to the cars we drive and the bridges we drive over. From the products we use and rely on, to the movies and games that inspire us. Autodesk's Design and Make Platform unlocks the power of data to accelerate insights and automate processes, empowering customers with the technology to create the world around us and deliver better outcomes for their businesses and the planet. Is Autodesk Still The Best Way To Own Faster Software Growth?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:52 PM CDT 4 min read
Autodesk (ADSK) stock lost 24.9% over the past year, while shares of Fair Isaac (FICO) fell 56.4%. Underneath those market declines, however, business at both software companies is accelerating. Each firm has posted faster sales growth in each of the past two years, and buyers of either stock are likely betting on that continued momentum. The similarities end there. The two companies operate with completely different financial structures. Fair Isaac retains far more of its sales as profit, yet Autodesk carries substantially less debt. So which of the two does the evidence favor?
In August, Autodesk Gave A Mixed Outlook
On August 27, Autodesk adjusted its expectations for the fiscal year ending in January 2027. The company raised its revenue forecast to a midpoint of $8.32 billion, up from $8.19 billion, and also increased its billings forecast. At the same time, it lowered its reported operating margin forecast down to 26.0% at the midpoint, from 27.0%.
Fair Isaac delivered a uniformly positive update on July 29, 2026. The company raised every forecast it gave for revenue, net income and earnings per share. For the fiscal year that ended in September 2026, management guided for $2.53 billion in revenue. Final results for that period are still to come.
Those optimistic projections arrived two months before a major industry announcement.
On September 28, the Federal Housing Finance Agency said the mortgage pricing grid is being simplified and that VantageScore is being incorporated. Fair Isaac stock fell after that statement the next day.
Autodesk Keeps Less Of Each Dollar, Holds More Cash
Looking at profitability, the two businesses operate in different tiers. Autodesk turned 27.9% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to July 2026. By contrast, Fair Isaac converted 52.1% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to June 2026.
When evaluating the balance sheet, Autodesk holds a commanding advantage. As of July 31, 2026, the company held $4.16 billion in cash and short-term investments, which easily exceeded its $3.71 billion of debt. Fair Isaac sits in a much tighter position. At June 30, 2026, the company owed $5.6 billion in debt against just $248 million of cash and short-term investments.
Fair Isaac trades at a notable discount relative to its bottom line. The stock trades at 20.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months. Investors are paying a higher premium for Autodesk, which trades at 29.6 times trailing earnings.
The top line also favors Fair Isaac. The company expanded sales by 24.1% over the twelve months to June 2026, easily outpacing the 17.9% growth Autodesk recorded over the twelve months to July 2026. Expanding the timeline reveals a similar pattern. Over its last three twelve-month periods, Fair Isaac averaged 17.7% growth, compared to 14.4% for Autodesk.
Autodesk reclaims the advantage regarding debt. The company carries debt equal to 7.6% of its market value. That sits well below the 34.4% ratio for Fair Isaac.
Based on its earnings multiple, growth, margin and forecasts, Fair Isaac comes out ahead, while Autodesk owes far less. The key variable remains timing. Fair Isaac issued its results and forecasts entirely before the agency's September move. The company expects to release its first report since that development on or around November 11, 2026. You should watch what Fair Isaac says about revenue in that report.
